newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury cuts back Lockheed contract.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury cuts back Lockheed contract.

text.p: The Treasury Department announced on Tuesday it was partly terminating a contract with Lockheed Martin for a document processing system for the Internal Revenue Service.

In a statement, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said: "We determined this project was not the best way to reliably improve customer service, increase productivity or help taxpayers comply with the system."
Treasury officials could not state the exact value of the original contract, which dates back to the 1980s and was intended to modernize and upgrade the tax collection system.
Published reports have estimated the contract was worth more than $1 billion.

IRS Commissioner Margaret Richardson said the first phase of the improved system was completed, but "given the revised priorities and budget realities of the next few years," Treasury had decided against spending more on it.
"Lockheed Martin's performance was not a factor in making this decision," Richardson said.
The IRS intends to invest in systems with a more direct and immediate effect on customer service, such as improved access to its toll-free telephone service, an official said.

Summers heads the Treasury's Modernization Management Board, which provides oversight for the tax updating program and reviews all major spending decisions. The Board ordered the IRS to do a detailed review of the project including the contract with Lockheed and then did a follow-up review of its own before deciding to partly terminate the contract.
